_comment: POS product name -> Purchase-module par SKU name.
WHY THIS FILE EXISTS: the till (Back Office sale products) and the Purchase
module (stock/par SKUs) are named by different people at different times and
they drift. The par model attributes POS volume to par SKUs BY NAME, so every
drifted name silently dropped 100% of that product's demand and the par
collapsed to whatever the safety net held it at.
The proven case: par SKU 'Petits Detours Rose Mediterranee - Bottle' (live par
22.9) only ever matched the POS line 'Petits Detours Rose Mediterranee'
(~3.9/wk, the by-the-bottle line). The by-the-glass line is called 'Petits
Detours Rose' (34.2/wk) and reached nothing, so 90% of the volume vanished and
the model recommended 3.0 for a wine that needs ~22.
Measured scale before this file existed: $54,794 of Stowaway drink sales over
13 weeks reached no par SKU at all.
FORMAT: "<POS product name>": "<par SKU name>", or, when the POS line is a
pour whose size the reporting group cannot imply,
"<POS product name>": {"sku": "<par SKU name>", "serve_ml": 150}.
RULES FOR ADDING AN ENTRY:
* Only map where you are CONFIDENT it is the same physical stock item.
* Glass/nip pour lines map to the '- Bottle' / '[Bottle]' / '[20L]' par SKU;
the model's existing unit conversion then applies. Do NOT pre-convert.
* Tap beer lines map to the '[Keg]' par SKU. schooner/pint -> keg conversion
is applied by the model (modules/par/model.py TAP_SERVE_ML).
* Made-to-order / post-mix drinks that consume no discrete stock unit go in
_intentionally_unattributed, NOT here.
* Cocktails belong to the RECIPE system (data/recipes/*.yaml), NOT here.
Enforced by the unattributed-volume coverage guard in
scripts/build_par_model.py, which fails the build if more than $2,000 of
13-week stock-bearing drink revenue reaches no par SKU.

stow.Fresh is Best Lager: House-brand tap lager. NOT a guess: data/recipes/stowaway.yaml defines 'Fresh is Best Lager - Schooner/- Pint' with the single ingredient 'Alehouse Draught Lager [Keg]'. Alehouse is the contract brewer; 'Fresh is Best' is the customer-facing name. The keg par SKU carried a live par of 4.6 with zero attributed volume, which is the drift signature.
stow.Fresh is Best Summer Lager: Same, via recipe 'Fresh is Best Summer Lager - Schooner/- Pint' -> 'Alehouse Summer Mid [Keg]' (live par 1.2, zero attributed volume).
stow.Guinness Draught: Only Guinness keg in the catalogue. resolve_bulk missed it purely on the trailing word 'Draught'.
stow.Philter Red: 'Philter Red [Keg]' exists in the catalogue but has no live par and no recipe; the POS line is 13.9/wk.
stow.Grifter - \"Omen\" Nitro Stout: Tap line -> 'Omen Stout Nitro [Keg]'. Deliberately NOT 'Grifter Omen Stout Tin' (live par 9.6): the POS line's reporting group is Tap Beer and the name says Nitro, so it is the keg, not the can.
stow.White Light Pure Vodka [House]: House-pour vodka on the 20L cask. The par SKU drops the word 'Pure'.
stow.Petits Detours Rosé: The by-the-glass line for the same wine. The bottle line 'Petits Detours Rosé Mediterranee' already matched; this one did not, and it is 90% of the volume.
stow.Baileys Irish Cream: Par SKU has an apostrophe and a '1L' size token.
stow.Vinada Sparkling Rose: TYPO IN THE PAR SKU NAME: 'Vinada Sparking Rosé [Bottle]' (missing the 'l' in Sparkling). Non-alc sparkling poured by the glass from a 750ml bottle - unit price $10.39 is a glass, and 4.1 glasses/wk against a live par of 0.6 bottles confirms it.
stow.Limoncello: The Liqueurs POS line (nip pour, $9.74) -> the only limoncello bottle in the par book. NOT 'Limoncello Spritz' (a cocktail, already resolved by the recipe book) and NOT the 'Limoncello Bottle - 250ml/700ml' delivery SKUs.
stow.Four Pillars Bloody Shiraz Gin Tonica: The '- Tonica' serve and the bare gin are the same bottle. The par SKUs drop the word 'Gin' ('Four Pillars Bloody Shiraz [Bottle]'), which is why the variant stripper alone could not bridge them.
stow.Kahlúa Coffee Liqueur: Par SKU is 'Kahlua [1L]' - no accent, no words 'Coffee Liqueur'. NOT 'Mr Black Coffee Liqueur [Bottle]', which is a different product the fuzzy matcher likes.
stow.Flor De Ca|a 4 Extra Seco: MOJIBAKE IN THE SOURCE: products_weekly.csv carries 'Ca|a' where the POS has 'Caña'. Mapped literally so the volume lands; fix the export encoding and this entry can go.
stow.Tequila Ocho - Single Estate A|ejo: Same mojibake ('A|ejo' = 'Añejo'), plus the par SKU spells it 'Anejo' without the tilde.
stow.4 Pines Kolsch Bottle: The only 4 Pines par SKU is the delivery twin '4 Pines Kolsch Bottle D'. Same physical bottle; the 'D' is a channel marker, not a different stock item.
stow.Bundaberg Ginger Beer: Par SKU carries the size token '[750ml]'.

hg.Harry's Lager: House tap lager. Recipe-proven: 'Harry's Lager - Schooner/- Pint/- Jug' -> 'Alehouse Premium Lager [Keg]'.
hg._no_alias_needed_Sapporo - 500ml: Deliberately NOT aliased. HG's recipe book already resolves 'Sapporo - 500ml' -> 'Sapporo [Keg]' at 500ml, and an alias would shadow a working recipe for no gain. The bare 'Sapporo' line is handled by the model's tap-beer pour path.
hg.S&W Pacific Ale: S&W = Stone & Wood; Pacific Ale is their flagship and 'Stone & Wood [Keg]' is the only S&W keg at HG.
hg.White Light Pure Vodka [House]: Note this is NOT the same target string as Stowaway's: HG's par SKU keeps the word 'Pure' ('White Light Pure Vodka [20L]'), Stowaway's drops it ('White Light Vodka [20L]'). Same drink, two different stock names - exactly the drift this file exists for.
hg.Kraken Black Rum: Par SKU is 'Kraken Rum [Bottle]' - the POS inserts 'Black'.
hg.Trutta Streamside Shiraz: By-the-glass line; the bottle par carries the '- Bottle [HG]' suffix.
hg.Two Tonne Riesling: By-the-glass line; the bottle par carries the '- Bottle [HG]' suffix.
hg.Vinada Sparkling Wine: 'Vinada Sparking Chardonnay [Bottle]' is the only Vinada stock item at HG (and note the same 'Sparking' typo as Stowaway's rosé). Low confidence on the varietal, high confidence on the stock item; revisit if HG ever carries two Vinadas.

These are poured from a post-mix gun or built to order from syrups and fresh produce; they consume NO discrete stock unit that the Purchase module carries a par for. They will never attribute, and the coverage guard must not nag about them forever.

_unmapped_investigate._comment: Stock-bearing POS lines with real volume that reach no par SKU and that I was NOT confident enough to map. These SHOULD be resolved by a human - either by creating the missing par SKU in the Purchase module or by confirming the mapping here. They still count toward the coverage guard's unattributed total, deliberately.
